panel_raw.steelman: The proposal's central doctrine move is correct and hard-won-lesson-aware. It refuses to add a "scientific assumption" trigger to the universal triage list (doctrine/proposals.md:154-177), correctly reads doctrine/rationale.md:337-347 as exhaustive to security + data-loss with "differentiator ⇒ high-risk" excluded (verified verbatim), correctly notes recurrence is uncounted, and correctly routes the science trigger through the existing per-project triage-extra-triggers slot whose placeholder already names "a domain assumption class the project guards" (template :48-54). That is the honest AND correct home — LESSON #4 respected. The automated-review-committer R1 precedent it invokes is faithful. Part 3's escape-hatch port is genuinely non-redundant: templates/core/AGENTS.md:76-79 and the installed template :39-40 both dead-end at a doctrine/ pointer the adopter lacks. Real gap, right mechanisms.

critiques.concern: Finding 5 presents a LOOSENED PARAPHRASE as a verbatim doctrine quote — the exact LESSON #1 failure mode. Proposal quotes the escape hatch as "urgent, reversible, or experimental may proceed without a proposal, but say why". Actual doctrine (verified) reads "urgent, clearly reversible, or explicitly experimental ... the commit or follow-up note should say why the proposal step was skipped." The paraphrase drops the tightening qualifiers "clearly"/"explicitly" and compresses the say-why clause — it BROADENS the escape hatch. Since Part 3 ports this exact text and invariant (iii) demands "no more and no less than" the doctrine, the implementer risks shipping the loosened version to every adopter.
critiques.suggested_fix: Quote doctrine/proposals.md:200-204 verbatim in finding 5, and state that Part 3's port must carry "clearly reversible", "explicitly experimental", and the full "say why the proposal step was skipped" clause — not the broadened paraphrase.

critiques.concern: Part 3 invokes the template's port exemption but does not satisfy the exemption's own stated condition. The exemption text requires that a porting proposal "cites the original accepting Decision and the gate does not re-apply." The proposal cites only the doctrine location (doctrine/proposals.md:200-204), not the Decision that originally accepted the escape hatch into doctrine. Without that citation the exemption is asserted, not established.
critiques.suggested_fix: Cite the accepting Decision for the escape-hatch rule; or, if it is foundational/pre-self-hosting doctrine with no discrete dev/ Decision, state that explicitly under the port-exemption invocation so a reviewer can see the exemption's condition is met (or waived for cause).

critiques.concern: Invariant (iii) claims the faithful-port property is "enforced by review reading, plus check_cairn staying clean." check_cairn does link + claim-path checking only (per AGENTS.md: it "imports the same claim-path checker and adds link-checking"); it structurally cannot detect semantic drift between the ported template paragraph and doctrine/proposals.md:200-204. This is exactly the duplication-drift failure doc-governance warns about ("copied into both files, later edited in one, and now silently contradictory"). The claimed automated guard does not exist — the only guard is one-time review reading.
critiques.grounding: doctrine/doc-governance.md:74-81 (drift failure mode); AGENTS.md check_cairn description
critiques.suggested_fix: Drop the check_cairn clause from invariant (iii); acknowledge there is no automated drift guard for template↔doctrine fidelity and that the port creates a small standing drift surface, mitigated only by keeping the ported text minimal and by review.

critiques.concern: The recipe's headline deliverable — a 'verified, copy-pasteable' YAML — does NOT parse for the zero-dependency adopter Cairn explicitly targets. The block puts inline comments on scalar lines (`preset: solo-greenfield   # ...`, `age: legacy   # ...`). config.py:34-43 uses PyYAML if present else `_minimal_yaml_parse`; the minimal parser strips comments on list items but NOT on scalar `key: value` lines. Reproduced this session: feeding the recipe's exact YAML to `_minimal_yaml_parse`+`expand_preset` raises `PresetError: unknown preset 'solo-greenfield     # solo staffing: one human + one agent'`. `age: legacy   #...` would likewise fail axis validation. No shipped profile inline-comments a scalar (grep over bootstrap/profiles/*.yml returned none); the recipe introduces the hazard. This hard-stops the first external adopter on day one with a confusing error — the exact failure the proposal exists to prevent.
critiques.grounding: Reproduced: python3 _minimal_yaml_parse(recipe.yml) -> age='legacy                 # ...'; expand_preset -> PresetError unknown preset. config.py:34-43 (parser selection); grep -nE '^[a-z_]+:[^#]*#' bootstrap/profiles/*.yml -> NONE.
critiques.suggested_fix: Move all comments to their own full lines (the shipped-profile convention), and re-verify the recipe YAML through `load_config`/`scaffold.py --config` under the stdlib-only path (not `expand_preset` on a hand-built dict). Have the Part 4 test exercise the YAML parse layer, not just `expand_preset`.

Worse: if the adopter scaffolds with `preset: solo-greenfield` (the quickstart pattern), install.py:736-738 renders solo-greenfield's onboarding tasks into PLANNING.md — 'Hello world trivial accept' (solo-greenfield.md:54-57) and 'no legacy-tree pre-pass' (solo-greenfield.md:28) — which directly contradict the recipe's week-one arc (assumptions.md-first + do the pre-pass). The recipe delivers its arc as external prose only and never reconciles the rendered tasks.
critiques.grounding: on-ramp/README.md:29 (Level 1 = no script); templates/onboarding/solo-greenfield.md:54-57 and :28; bootstrap/_scaffold/install.py:736-738; templates/core/dev/PLANNING.md:33,43 (slot filled by bootstrap, empty at hand-copy).

critiques.concern: The recipe force-adds security-review and model-selection into the canonical 10-module roster, but both FAIL their own selection gates for this persona, and doing so pre-empts the readiness-report pre-pass the same recipe prescribes. security-review is trust-boundary-first ('a place where untrusted input meets the system: deserialization, subprocess, file/network I/O, path handling, credential/env use') — a solo hydrogeology recharge model reading its own input data typically has no non-trivial trust boundary. model-selection is 'Selected when the project sits at moderate or complex on the Complexity axis... A greenfield experimental project at low complexity does not install this module' — yet the recipe keeps complexity:simple (solo-greenfield canonical, never overridden by the recipe YAML) and force-adds it anyway. The recipe's whole framing is 'readiness-report pre-pass first' to discover complexity/trust-boundaries/hidden-state, then hands the adopter a FIXED modules_add that decides those very questions before the pre-pass runs. This is precisely the over-provisioning Cairn's own cited doctrine warns against.
critiques.grounding: templates/modules/team-gated/security-review.md:3-11 (trust-boundary-first gate); templates/modules/team-gated/model-selection.md:3-9 ('greenfield experimental project at low complexity does not install this module'); verified via expand_preset that the recipe YAML sets only preset/age/modules_add so complexity stays 'simple'; doctrine/dual-review.md:442 ('never installs more apparatus than the team can staff'); on-ramp/README.md:40 ('sized to the work'); templates/modules/team-gated/testing-discipline.md:5-7 ('not every adoption paying for it by default')

critiques.concern: Part 3 (porting the escape-hatch paragraph into templates/core/dev/proposals/_template.md) has a broader beneficiary scope than Parts 1/2/4 and is separable. So the 'one spine' claim is overstated: three parts serve one persona, one is a general template improvement riding along. Three reasons: (1) the proposal itself names recipe prose readability/followability as unmechanizable and 'ideally sampled by the cross-type External read' — that surface is unverifiable until the doc exists and is exactly what a different reader-type catches; (2) this is literally the first-external-adopter's day-one path, the highest-stakes usability surface in the repo right now; (3) my strongest finding (proportionality — force-adding security-review/model-selection against their own gates) is a judgment call about what a real solo postdoc needs versus ceremony they will bounce off, precisely the 'does this help or add load' question a different agent type is likelier to weigh independently. Per the maintainer's cross-type workflow, the standing External is the Antigravity/Gemini reviewer. My proportionality and Part-3-scope findings should be addressed (or consciously rejected) in a Response before that External read, so it evaluates the sharpened recipe rather than re-deriving the same gaps.

consolidated.steelman: All three lenses converge: this is an unusually well-verified proposal and a model of navigating Cairn's known failure modes. The empirical spine is solid and independently reproduces across lenses — re-running expand_preset confirms exactly: naive {preset: solo-greenfield, age: legacy} -> the 6 default-on modules with no legacy-agent and no warning (config.py:1143-1148 static-baseline mechanism); +complexity:complex/language:multi -> still 6; and the recipe composition -> the documented 10-module roster in the exact printed order with zero staffability warnings. Every doctrine quote is faithful (rationale.md:337-347/346-347/327-329; proposals.md:154-177/200-204; readiness-report:295/299-302/363-367), and Findings 1-6 are real and reproduce. The rate-limit reasoning is honest and correct: it refuses the gate-blocked universal-triage doctrine change, reads doctrine/rationale.md:337-347 as exhaustive to security + data-loss with "differentiator => high-risk" excluded (verified verbatim), notes recurrence is uncounted, and routes the science trigger through the existing per-project triage-extra-triggers slot whose placeholder already names "a domain assumption class the project guards" (template:48-54) — the honest AND correct home, so slot-fill is not a doctrine change; LESSON #4 respected and the automated-review-committer R1 precedent faithfully invoked. Part 3's escape-hatch port is genuinely non-redundant: templates/core/AGENTS.md:76-79 and the installed template :39-40 both dead-end at a doctrine/ pointer the adopter lacks — real gap, right mechanisms. The work is built only from shipped mechanisms with no engine change (AST re-anchor correctly not triggered), and it defers the engine fix, the Appendix-B fix, and the first-class preset to their own proposals — respecting the anti-bundling and rate-limit lessons that killed prior proposals. The docs/assumptions.md week-one arc targets the differentiator well.

numbered_critiques.concern: The recipe's headline deliverable — a 'verified, copy-pasteable' YAML — does NOT parse for the zero-dependency adopter Cairn explicitly targets. The block puts inline comments on scalar lines (`preset: solo-greenfield   # ...`, `age: legacy   # ...`); config.py:34-43 uses PyYAML if present else `_minimal_yaml_parse`, and the minimal parser strips comments on list items but NOT on scalar `key: value` lines, so it hard-stops the first external adopter on day one with a confusing PresetError — the exact failure the proposal exists to prevent. Same defect, its root cause: the verification that produced the 'verified' claim never exercised the adopter path — 'Already exercised manually this session via expand_preset' bypasses YAML parsing entirely (expand_preset takes a pre-parsed dict), and this environment has PyYAML 6.0.3, so the plan's end-to-end dogfood passes silently and masks the failure; Part 4 tests roster math via expand_preset(dict), giving no coverage of the copy-pasteability claim that is the recipe's core value.
numbered_critiques.grounding: Reproduced: python3 _minimal_yaml_parse(recipe.yml) -> age='legacy                 # ...'; expand_preset -> PresetError unknown preset 'solo-greenfield     # solo staffing: ...'; config.py:34-43 (parser selection); grep -nE '^[a-z_]+:[^#]*#' bootstrap/profiles/*.yml -> NONE (no shipped profile inline-comments a scalar). Plus: proposal text 'Already exercised manually this session via expand_preset'; `import yaml` succeeds here (PyYAML 6.0.3); config.py:34-43 shows the PyYAML branch masks the minimal-parser behavior.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Move all comments to their own full lines (the shipped-profile convention), and re-verify the recipe YAML through `load_config`/`scaffold.py --config` under the stdlib-only path (not `expand_preset` on a hand-built dict). Run the dogfood explicitly under the no-PyYAML path (or force `_minimal_yaml_parse`), and have Part 4 add a case that round-trips the recipe's literal YAML text through `load_config`, asserting the 10-module roster — pinning copy-pasteability, not just the resolver.

numbered_critiques.concern: Finding 5 presents a LOOSENED PARAPHRASE as a verbatim doctrine quote — the exact LESSON #1 failure mode. The proposal quotes the escape hatch as 'urgent, reversible, or experimental may proceed without a proposal, but say why'. Actual doctrine (verified) reads 'urgent, clearly reversible, or explicitly experimental ... the commit or follow-up note should say why the proposal step was skipped.' The paraphrase drops the tightening qualifiers 'clearly'/'explicitly' and compresses the say-why clause — it BROADENS the escape hatch. Since Part 3 ports this exact text and invariant (iii) demands 'no more and no less than' the doctrine, the implementer risks shipping the loosened version to every adopter.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Quote doctrine/proposals.md:200-204 verbatim in finding 5, and state that Part 3's port must carry 'clearly reversible', 'explicitly experimental', and the full 'say why the proposal step was skipped' clause — not the broadened paraphrase.

numbered_critiques.concern: The recipe force-adds security-review and model-selection into the canonical 10-module roster, but both FAIL their own selection gates for this persona, and doing so pre-empts the readiness-report pre-pass the same recipe prescribes. security-review is trust-boundary-first ('a place where untrusted input meets the system: deserialization, subprocess, file/network I/O, path handling, credential/env use') — a solo hydrogeology recharge model reading its own input data typically has no non-trivial trust boundary. model-selection is 'Selected when the project sits at moderate or complex on the Complexity axis... A greenfield experimental project at low complexity does not install this module' — yet the recipe keeps complexity:simple (solo-greenfield canonical, never overridden by the recipe YAML) and force-adds it anyway. The recipe's whole framing is 'readiness-report pre-pass first' to discover complexity/trust-boundaries/hidden-state, then hands the adopter a FIXED modules_add that decides those very questions before the pre-pass runs — precisely the over-provisioning Cairn's own cited doctrine warns against.
numbered_critiques.grounding: templates/modules/team-gated/security-review.md:3-11 (trust-boundary-first gate); templates/modules/team-gated/model-selection.md:3-9 ('greenfield experimental project at low complexity does not install this module'); verified via expand_preset that the recipe YAML sets only preset/age/modules_add so complexity stays 'simple'; doctrine/dual-review.md:442 ('never installs more apparatus than the team can staff'); on-ramp/README.md:40 ('sized to the work'); templates/modules/team-gated/testing-discipline.md:5-7 ('not every adoption paying for it by default')
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Split modules_add into (a) the two the persona unconditionally needs — legacy-agent (the actual finding-2 gap) + testing-discipline (pairs with the characterization-testing age.md:52-54 prescribes for legacy) — and (b) security-review / model-selection presented as CONDITIONAL, keyed to pre-pass findings ('add security-review IF your readiness report flags a trust boundary; add model-selection IF complexity is moderate+'). This makes the recipe teach the sizing discipline instead of contradicting it; both subsets still resolve without staffability warnings.

numbered_critiques.concern: The recipe is internally inconsistent about adoption level, and its first-proposal / week-one arc contradicts the onboarding tasks solo-greenfield actually renders. (a) Part 1 says 'Level 1 (hand-copy the kernel)', but on-ramp/README.md:29 defines Level 1 as 'No bootstrap script', while the recipe delivers a scaffold profile + `modules_add` + `scaffold.py --summary` (Level-2 machinery); and if the adopter scaffolds with `preset: solo-greenfield` (the quickstart pattern), install.py:736-738 renders solo-greenfield's onboarding tasks into PLANNING.md — 'Hello world trivial accept' (solo-greenfield.md:54-57) and 'no legacy-tree pre-pass' (solo-greenfield.md:28) — which directly contradict the recipe's week-one arc (assumptions.md-first + do the pre-pass), and the recipe delivers its arc as external prose only and never reconciles the rendered tasks. (b) Relatedly, promoting docs/assumptions.md to the 'default first real proposal' in place of the greenfield Hello-world removes the low-stakes first rep that teaches the lifecycle mechanics safely — solo-greenfield's first proposal is deliberately a 'Hello world'-style TRIVIAL accept ('the single best way to learn the apparatus by doing'); docs/assumptions.md is a real, non-trivial, science-laden artifact, so making it the postdoc's very first lifecycle experience runs their first-ever review/Decision loop on content that matters, and the readiness report's own conditional says assumptions.md should be the first ACCEPTED proposal, not the first-ever learning rep.
numbered_critiques.grounding: on-ramp/README.md:29 (Level 1 = no script); templates/onboarding/solo-greenfield.md:54-57 and :28; bootstrap/_scaffold/install.py:736-738; templates/core/dev/PLANNING.md:33,43 (slot filled by bootstrap, empty at hand-copy); templates/codebase-readiness-report.md:363-367 (Section-11-Poor conditional: assumptions.md as first artifact)
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: State the flow explicitly. If scaffold-install: instruct the adopter to override the rendered 'Hello world'/'no pre-pass' onboarding task and acknowledge the conflict. If pure hand-copy: label `--summary`/`modules_add` as a roster-computation oracle (what to copy), not the installer, and reconcile with on-ramp:29. And sequence the first proposals rather than replace: Hello-world trivial accept FIRST to learn the mechanics on something disposable, THEN docs/assumptions.md as the first SUBSTANTIVE proposal — reframe from 'in place of the Hello world' to 'after the Hello world.'

numbered_critiques.concern: Invariant (iii) claims the faithful-port property ('the escape-hatch paragraph says no more and no less than doctrine/proposals.md:200-204') is 'enforced by review reading, plus check_cairn staying clean' — but check_cairn does link + claim-path checking only (per AGENTS.md it 'imports the same claim-path checker and adds link-checking') and structurally cannot detect semantic drift between the ported template paragraph and doctrine; the claimed automated guard does not exist, and the port creates exactly the duplication-drift failure doc-governance warns about ('copied into both files, later edited in one, and now silently contradictory'). Part 3 also breaks the template's deliberate pointer-only convention (template:39-40, :58-60, :68-69 all say 'See doctrine/... for the full rule'), creating a duplicate-text drift surface — the very thing pointer-only avoids.
numbered_critiques.grounding: doctrine/doc-governance.md:74-81 (drift failure mode); AGENTS.md check_cairn description; templates/core/dev/proposals/_template.md:39-40 (existing escape-hatch pointer), :58-60, :68-69 (pointer convention); doctrine/proposals.md:200-204
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Drop the check_cairn clause from invariant (iii); correct the verification plan to state the port is enforced by review reading, not check_cairn, and acknowledge there is no automated drift guard for template<->doctrine fidelity — the port creates a small standing drift surface, mitigated only by keeping the ported text minimal and by review. Prefer keeping the pointer plus a short local gloss (finding-5's real need: adopters lack doctrine/ locally) over a full restatement; or add an explicit sync-note so a future doctrine edit re-syncs the template copy.

numbered_critiques.concern: Part 3 invokes the template's port exemption but does not satisfy the exemption's own stated condition. The exemption text requires that a porting proposal 'cites the original accepting Decision and the gate does not re-apply.' The proposal cites only the doctrine location (doctrine/proposals.md:200-204), not the Decision that originally accepted the escape hatch into doctrine. Without that citation the exemption is asserted, not established.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Cite the accepting Decision for the escape-hatch rule; or, if it is foundational/pre-self-hosting doctrine with no discrete dev/ Decision, state that explicitly under the port-exemption invocation so a reviewer can see the exemption's condition is met (or waived for cause).

numbered_critiques.concern: Part 3 (porting the escape-hatch paragraph into templates/core/dev/proposals/_template.md) has a broader beneficiary scope than Parts 1/2/4 and is separable: Parts 1, 2, 4 all serve the solo-legacy persona, but Part 3 edits the UNIVERSAL installed proposal template every adopter gets and the escape hatch benefits all adopters equally — so the 'one spine' claim is overstated. Further, finding-5's own logic (the adopter lacks doctrine/ locally) applies to EVERY 'See doctrine/...' pointer in that template — including the triage-rule pointer at :39-40, arguably more important than the escape hatch — so singling out the escape hatch is a partial fix to a systematic dangling-pointer problem. This is not the fatal new-tool-vs-fixes bundling (all four parts are low-risk prose/test), so it need not force a split, but the Maintainer should be able to accept/reject Part 3 independently.
numbered_critiques.grounding: templates/core/dev/proposals/_template.md:39-40 (an existing 'See doctrine/...' pointer that also dangles for adopters lacking doctrine/) and :48-54 (the slot); the escape-hatch text lives canonically at doctrine/proposals.md:200-204
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Either carve Part 3 out as its own trivial follow-up commit (it is a pure doctrine-text port, cleanly separable), or broaden it to address the systematic dangling-doctrine-pointer issue in the template — and in either case state explicitly that Part 3 is independently acceptable, so the Maintainer isn't forced to take the general template change to get the persona recipe.

numbered_critiques.concern: Part 2 overstates the on-ramp routing gap by omitting an existing mechanism that already partly solves it. The choosing-a-level section already maps a legacy solo project via the readiness report's G/M/P scores — 'mostly Mixed with 1-2 Poor -> Level 1 first' — i.e. the legacy->Level 1 route Part 2 proposes already exists in finer-grained form; only the coarse table row (:63) contradicts 'solo -> Level 1'. Presenting the routing as wholly broken misstates the negative space.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Cite on-ramp/README.md:52-57 and scope Part 2 as reconciling the coarse table row with the existing G/M/P mapping (and cross-linking the recipe), not as adding a missing route.

numbered_critiques.concern: Finding 3 (the Appendix B / I-6 summary three-of-six default-on drift) is deferred as a separate risk class, but it is a pure factual doc error in the SAME document the recipe leans on for its 'compose, don't bypass' authority (BOOTSTRAP.md:188). Verified live: BOOTSTRAP.md:696-698 lists only 3 of the 6 default-on modules, :215 repeats it, and cli.py:348-353 (the 'modules:' branch) emits no missing-default-on warning — so any adopter who wanders off the recipe to Appendix B silently under-installs. This is the same risk class as an adopter-facing doc recipe (not an engine change), and the fix is ~3 lines in 2 places; the anti-bundling lesson does not clearly bar folding it in, and the recipe should not send the postdoc to a doc containing a known-wrong hand-derivation example.
numbered_critiques.grounding: bootstrap/BOOTSTRAP.md:696-698 and :215 (both list only 3 of the 6 default-on modules; the full set is lifecycle-metrics, reflections, claim-check, fold-back-ledger, incident-trackers, documentation-plan per _DEFAULT_ON_MODULES); bootstrap/_scaffold/cli.py:348-353 (the 'modules:' branch prints no missing-default-on warning) vs :356-364 (else-branch prints the default-on set)
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Consider folding the finding-3 doc-sync into scope as a bounded same-class factual correction (the proposal's own 'signals' section already anticipates this), or land it as a separate trivial commit BEFORE the install so the recipe's host document is not self-contradicting.

numbered_critiques.concern: Finding 1 overstates one sub-claim: it says bootstrap-lite.md:8 routes the solo persona 'to the Level 2 scaffold'. But bootstrap-lite.md:5-6 is explicitly for adopting Cairn 'without running the full Level 2 procedure in ../BOOTSTRAP.md yet' — it is a heavier middle on-ramp, not the Level 2 scaffold. The core finding (bootstrap-lite targets one-human+one-agent yet is gated on 'you have a real codebase', so the persona is mis-served) is verified and stands; only the 'Level 2 scaffold' characterization is inaccurate.
numbered_critiques.grounding: bootstrap/prompts/bootstrap-lite.md:1 (one-human+one-agent), :5-6 ('without running the full Level 2 procedure'), :8 ('you have a real codebase')
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Reword finding 1 to say bootstrap-lite is a heavier middle path gated on 'you have a real codebase', not that it routes to the Level 2 scaffold.

numbered_critiques.concern: Doc-tier label imprecision: the routing note calls Part 2 'descriptive layer (on-ramp/).' DOCUMENTATION_PLAN.md's four-layer map locates the descriptive layer at docs/ (layer 4) and defines the entry layer by the 'how do I enter?' question, which is what on-ramp self-locate content answers. No gate consequence (on-ramp/ is not doctrine either way), but the classification is inaccurate.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Reclassify Part 2's surface as entry/on-ramp, or note that on-ramp/ is not formally placed in the four-layer map; either way confirm no doctrine gate applies.

numbered_critiques.concern: Two concerns about how the proposal handles the deferred silent engine bug (finding 2). (a) The recipe exposes that acknowledged silent engine bug to the adopter as first-contact content: Part 1's 'Why not the naive age: legacy override alone' callout explains, to a postdoc on day one, that the tool has a silent under-install path they must hand-work-around — maintainer-facing concern, not adoption-path content — which adds cognitive load and undermines confidence at the exact moment the adopter is deciding whether to trust the tool; the paired 'confirm the --summary roster matches the documented 10' step is a verification chore whose failure mode (mismatch) a moderate-git postdoc cannot diagnose. (b) Part 4's regression test pins finding-2's behavior (age override does NOT re-derive age-gated rows) as a baseline, but finding 2 is simultaneously flagged as a bug deferred to its own engine-fix proposal (Alternative 4); if that fix later lands (making the override re-derive), invariant (ii) goes red — which the proposal calls 'intended,' but a future implementer could mistake it for a regression.
numbered_critiques.grounding: The recipe's own Part 1 text ('a short, honest callout of finding 2, so the adopter understands why the modules_add lines are load-bearing'); finding 2's mechanism verified at bootstrap/_scaffold/config.py:1143-1148 (baseline is static + default-on + team-staffing re-derive only); the proposal's Part 4 / Evidence invariant (ii) ('the naive {solo-greenfield, age:legacy} resolves to the 6 default-on modules... pinned so any future change to it is a deliberate diff'); the deferred fix is Alternative 4 ('Fix the engine so an age override re-derives age-gated baseline rows')
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Keep the modules_add workaround but frame those lines positively as 'the legacy-retrofit modules for an existing codebase' rather than 'the ones the override silently fails to add'; move the finding-2 mechanism explanation to a footnote/rationale aside for the curious, not the main path. And make the Part 4 test comment state explicitly that it pins CURRENT behavior pending the deferred finding-2 engine fix (Alt 4), not a desired invariant — so a future implementer who lands that fix knows the red is expected and updates the test as part of that change.

consolidated.second_round_recommendation: Yes — all three lenses recommend an External cross-type read before the Decision, matching the proposal's own request; scope-adopter would elevate it from "recommended" to effectively expected for this one. Reasons converge: (1) the blocking YAML-parse defect (R1) must be fixed and re-verified through the stdlib-only path before landing, and an independent read should confirm the fix rather than trust a re-run in this PyYAML-present environment; (2) the Level-1-vs-scaffold flow, the onboarding-task conflict (R4), and the routing/usability gaps sit on the exact path the first external adopter walks — routing/usability judgments a different agent type catches best; (3) recipe prose readability/followability is a named plan-review criterion no scanner reaches, unverifiable until the doc exists, best sampled by the cross-type reviewer. Per the maintainer's cross-type workflow, the standing External is the Antigravity/Gemini reviewer. Two sequencing notes: the proportionality finding (R3) and the Part-3-scope finding (R7) should be addressed — or consciously rejected — in a Response BEFORE the External read, so it evaluates the sharpened recipe rather than re-deriving the same gaps; and the one residual engine-verification item is the full `scaffold.py --summary` end-to-end path (the roster itself is already confirmed via expand_preset across two lenses). The doctrine findings are all tightening, not blocking, and none requires a doctrine-gate re-litigation.
